newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Union rejects Portugal 2.4 pct public sector offer.
newsitem.headline: Union rejects Portugal 2.4 pct public sector offer.

text.p: Portugal's Socialist government has offered public sector employees wage rises of 2.375 percent for 1997 but the largest union dismissed the proposal as a "near provocation".
The offer was announced on Wednesday night after a first round of wage talks between government officials and union leaders.
Unions are asking for rises of between 4.5 and seven percent for some 500,000 public sector employees whose wage deals usually set the trend for salaries in the private sector.

Carlos Mamede, head of the Frente Commun, the Communist-led union group which is the largest in the public sector, said that the offer failed to meet any of the unions' demands and was "a near provocation."
No date has been set yet for further talks.

The government says that Portugal can only offer very moderate wage rises next year if it is to meet tough targets on inflation and the budget deficit set for entry to the European Union's proposed monetary union.
Prime Minister Antonio Guterres has made qualifying amongst the first group of EU countries to wed their economies in a single currency his top policy priority.
The offered wage increase was in the middle of the government's forecast for inflation next year of 2.25-2.5 percent.
